target_condition.evidence_quote: MTX, a first-line rheumatoid arthritis (RA) treatment... RA patient microbiotas were sensitive to MTX

body_site.evidence_quote: stool samples collected from a healthy human male (Donor 1)
body_site.notes: Fecal samples used for microbiota analysis throughout study

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_exclusion_period.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: Exclusion criterion applied to RA patient cohort

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: MoBio Powersoil DNA extraction kit; ZymoBIOMICS 96 MagBead DNA Kit
dna_extraction_kit.section: STAR Methods — 16S-seq of humanized mouse gut microbiota
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Multiple kits used: MoBio PowerSoil and Zymo BIOMICS; both available but not in enum

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: All sequencing data generated in the preparation of this manuscript has been deposited in NCBI's Sequence Read Archive (SRA), under Bioproject ID PRJNA656577

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: The V4 hypervariable region of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) was performed using a MiSeq Illumina platform
sequencing_platform.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
sequencing_platform.notes: Also used IlluminaNovaSeq in some experiments; MiSeq is primary platform for 16S

subject_id.notes: Individual subject/participant IDs not provided; only donor designations (Donor 1, 2, 3) and cohort numbers (n=30 MTX-naïve patients, n=23 RA patients)

sample_id.notes: Specific sample IDs not provided; samples referenced by experiment, timepoint, and donor

country.evidence_quote: Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics
country.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
country.notes: NYU Langone is in New York, USA

age.notes: Individual participant ages not reported; only inclusion criterion ≥18 years mentioned

sex.notes: Sex reported for individual donors (Donor 1 male; Donor 2 and 3 female and male re-MTX patients) but not for larger RA cohort

ancestry.notes: Ancestry information not provided in paper

westernized.evidence_quote: New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics
westernized.section: STAR Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
westernized.notes: Inferred from NYC-based urban medical center recruitment; no explicit statement

control.notes: RA patients are cases; healthy donor (Donor 1) functions as control but not explicitly labeled in sample metadata

zigosity.notes: No twin zygosity information reported in paper

age_min.notes: Mice were 6-16 weeks old; human age not reported for most cohorts

age_max.notes: Only age range for mice reported (6-16 weeks)

age_years.notes: Human participant ages not reported in methods or tables; mouse ages given in weeks

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_current_use.section: EXPERIMENTAL MODEL AND SUBJECT DETAILS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion specified recent antibiotic use within 3 months

bmi.notes: BMI not reported for any human participants

dietary_restriction.notes: Diet exclusion criteria specified extreme diet but no specific dietary restrictions reported

disease.evidence_quote: Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics and offices were screened for the presence of RA based on ACR criteria
disease.section: EXPERIMENTAL MODEL AND SUBJECT DETAILS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
disease.notes: RA defined by American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism 2010 classification criteria

disease_details.evidence_quote: New-onset RA was defined as disease duration of a minimum of 6 weeks and up to 6 months since diagnosis
disease_details.section: EXPERIMENTAL MODEL AND SUBJECT DETAILS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
disease_details.notes: NORA patients had 6 weeks to 6 months disease duration at baseline

disease_response_orr.notes: Overall Response Rate (ORR) not reported; DAS28 response used instead

disease_response_pfs.notes: Progression-Free Survival not applicable; RA response measured by DAS28 score change

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: PFS not measured; follow-up at 4 months post-treatment

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST criteria not applicable; RA study used DAS28 response criteria

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: Stool samples were collected at baseline and 1 month after MTX initiation
feces_phenotype.section: EXPERIMENTAL MODEL AND SUBJECT DETAILS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
feces_phenotype.notes: Fecal samples collected at baseline and post-treatment timepoints

fmt_id.notes: No study-specific FMT participant identifiers reported; donors identified as Donor 1-6

fmt_role.evidence_quote: Germ-free mice were colonized with pre- and post-treatment stool samples from the 3 MTX-Rs
fmt_role.section: RESULTS — The post-treatment microbiome decreases host immune activation
fmt_role.notes: Gnotobiotic mice received FMT from RA patients; human donors provided stool for microbiota transplantation

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Gestational age at birth not reported for human participants

smoker.notes: Smoking status not reported; smoking mentioned as potential confounding factor in discussion

treatment.evidence_quote: Patients received oral MTX at standard of care doses as prescribed by their treating rheumatologists
treatment.section: EXPERIMENTAL MODEL AND SUBJECT DETAILS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
treatment.notes: MTX dosing by treating rheumatologists; doses varied by standard of care

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: AJCC tumor staging not applicable; study focuses on RA not cancer

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: TNM staging not applicable; study focuses on RA not cancer

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Bacteroidetes decreased; purine and pyrimidine metabolism were among top pathways; B220+, Foxp3+ CD4+, CD44+ CD69+ CD4+, Gr1+ CD11b+ cells were significantly lower
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified as indicators of MTX effects on microbiota and immune response across different experimental models.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: fold change relative to pre-MTX recipients; percentage of cells; p adj <0.05
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type; mostly relative measurements or statistical p-values.

value: 18 positive correlations, 1 negative correlation in spleen
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Bacteroidetes decreased (slope=−0.066, p=0.007); 0.48–1.3 fold change; 0.64 – 1.33 fold change; DAS28 of ≥1.8
biomarker_value.notes: Specific numerical values extracted from results reporting biomarker measurements.

disease_response_os.notes: This paper focuses on microbiota and immune response biomarkers in RA patients; overall survival is not a reported outcome measure.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; overall survival not measured in this study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not assessed or reported in this study.

value: Decreased Bacteroidetes phylum with MTX treatment
Decreased microbial richness with MTX exposure
Shifted community structure after 1 day (ANOSIM R=0.60, p=0.006)
Altered 14 bacterial genera and 81 ASVs with high-dose MTX
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: High-dose MTX significantly decreased Bacteroidetes; MTX significantly altered gut microbial community after 1 day; 14 bacterial genera and 81 amplicon sequence variants
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes measured via 16S rRNA sequencing; multiple compositional and structural changes reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: This is a microbiota and immunology study in rheumatoid arthritis patients; tumor size measurement not applicable.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; study does not involve tumor assessment.

value: Study involves germ-free mice colonized with human microbiota
MTX doses tested: 1 mg/kg (low-dose) and 50 mg/kg (high-dose) in mice
RA patients treated with standard oral MTX doses
Clinical responders defined as DAS28 decrease ≥1.8 with continued MTX use
45 bacterial isolates from 6 phyla tested for MTX sensitivity
Minimal Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) ranged across full gradient tested (1.7-900 μg/ml)
Estimated MTX concentration in proximal GI tract: 22-220 μM (10-100 μg/ml)
DSS used as inflammatory trigger in transplant experiments
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: germ-free mice colonized with stool; 1 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg; 25 mg oral MTX; DAS28 decrease ≥1.8; 45 bacterial isolates; 1.7–900 μg/ml; 22–220 μM; DSS treatment
uncurated_metadata.notes: Additional experimental parameters and design details relevant to understanding the study context.

host_species.evidence_quote: stool samples obtained from 30 MTX-naïve patients; C57BL/6J mice (females, ages 6–16 weeks)
host_species.notes: Study includes both human RA patients and germ-free laboratory mice colonized with human microbiota.
